key.description: The resource's identity, when that is not its path. Say it when you move the file: the path the resource had. It never changes.

path.description: The resource's path, when the file is kept somewhere that does not give it one.

entry.description: The file, among the app's files in the bundle, that is the page itself.

interface.description: An interface of the workspace to serve as this app, in place of files of its own. An app has an entry, an interface or docs, and only one of them.

docs.description: A top-level folder of the workspace's pages of documentation to serve as this app: every page whose path is under it. Its `index` page is the home page, each folder directly under it is a collection, and folders go as deep as they are written.

feedback.description: For an app that serves documentation: ask readers whether a page helped, and keep each answer as a row of a table of the workspace's. The table has exactly the columns `site_key` (text, the key of the site's app), `site` (text), `page` (text), `helpful` (boolean), `version` (text) and `at` (timestamp). A reader answers once for each page, and nothing about who they are is kept.

table.description: The table the answers are kept in.

published.description: For an app that serves documentation: false stops serving it, and keeps its pages and the app. It is served again once this is left out or true, from the next deploy. Default true.

fallback.description: Whether an address under the app that names no file answers with the entry page, for apps that route in the browser. Default true.

reads.description: The tables the app's code reads, so that whoever shares it can see what it reaches. It informs; the tables' policies and the app's bindings are what decide access.
